# Go optimizer shared fixtures and receipts

The core JSON fixtures are deliberately synthetic contract data. The named
GOB receipts additionally preserve compact facts from the current real context
without storing its multi-megabyte payloads. Formula-search values are not
n=1000 gameplay claims. Files are pinned so identity or arithmetic changes
require an explicit contract decision.

The fixture uses twenty artifacts only to exercise the real Selected physical
shape: four wearers, five canonical slots each, and globally unique IDs. Real
receipts keep or intentionally version this process boundary.

`gob2_frozen_seed_receipt_v1.json` is the compact immutable receipt of that
GOB-2 adapter proof. It preserves hashes, parity, size, and runtime facts
without making temporary multi-megabyte traces permanent test inputs.

`gob3a_stochastic_contract_v1.json` freezes the two-seed development panel,
equal-weight arithmetic, dispersion, uncertainty, baseline, and non-authority
rules before the Go aggregator is implemented.

`gob3d_two_seed_capture_receipt_v1.json` records the two real compact members
captured sequentially from the isolated 0001-0022 staging engine. It preserves
their identities and baseline validation without committing the multi-megabyte
member payloads.

`gob3e_real_panel_parity_receipt_v1.json`, `gob3f_runtime_receipt_v1` and
`gob4_indexed_evaluator_receipt_v1.json` freeze real two-member arithmetic,
runtime and indexed-domain parity without storing the 9.28 MB payload.

`gob5_python_reference_v1.json` is the smallest migration witness for the old
Python leader. `gob5_real_account_acceptance_receipt_v1.json` proves that clean
Go FGBS retains it, finds a no-worse same-panel leader and stays below the
190-second search boundary. Neither receipt is an n=1000 gameplay result.

`gob7_common_n1000_acceptance_receipt_v1.json` is the first measured Selected
gameplay receipt. It freezes the common n=128 screen, bounded common n=1000
finalists, exact twenty-ID winner, Current comparison, residual and cold
170.67-second product runtime without retaining private full engine outputs.

`gob8p_exact_seven_n500_receipt_v1.json` records the one permitted isolated
performance replay. It reused exactly the seven saved finalists, skipped
formula search and n=128, preserved the saved n=1000 winner and top-five set,
and cut final verification from 92.54 to 46.36 seconds. It supports a bounded
adaptive final gate; it does not claim that n=500 precisely orders close
runner-up rows.

`gob8p_adaptive_acceptance_receipt_v1.json` records the subsequent single full
Go acceptance. Common n=128 retained the known winner, the seven-row adaptive
panel resolved at n=500 without extension, and the complete Go boundary
finished in 159.06 seconds with the same exact winner identity.

`all_sets_two_stage_benchmark_v1.json` is the rejected N1 priority-first
scheduler witness: it was faster than the incumbent but lost the accepted
winner, so that ordering was removed. `all_sets_two_stage_benchmark_v2.json`
is the accepted saved-request backend comparison for the fair six-context
scout/deepen coordinator. It preserves the exact20-artifact winner and formula
while reducing native time from491.81 to403.04 seconds. Neither receipt is an
additional visible-UI acceptance or a universal speed guarantee.

Finite-energy acceptance is intentionally kept in executable regressions rather
than a large private capture fixture. The engine ledger, Go deadline model,
formula-invisible ER search, ordinary insufficient-energy rejection and product
formatter have focused tests. The saved Chasca/Furina/Ororon/Bennett control is
summarized in `GCSIM_GOB11_GP3_CHECKPOINT.md`: its selected-set inventory is
provably infeasible under the observed two-seed schedule, so no winner is
reported. Do not turn that account-specific result into a universal ER rule.

`optimizer_mode_matrix_account_v1.json` is the compact 2026-09-17 account
review receipt for the three product modes. It records Chasca, Lunar-Charged
and Bloom teams, two different Flins/Sucrose rotations, the first seven
reported candidates and adapter timings without retaining expanded captures.
The probe instantiates the same request/session classes as the Qt worker and
uses managed scratch. It is backend evidence, not a native visible-button
acceptance or a proof that the reported alternatives are globally exhaustive.

`optimizer_archetype_full_matrix_lineage5_20260919.json` records 14 virtual
rosters in All Sets and Theory: per-mode elapsed time, five result summaries,
physical artifact IDs and main stats, formula-channel coordinates, bounded
Theory proposals, warnings and four engine-identity fields. It is the compact
output of `tools/experiments/gcsim/mode_matrix/run_product_matrix.py`; the
runner's owned scratch (including the read-only account copy) is removed on
exit. The dated analysis and actual application-button scope are in
`docs/handoff/GCSIM_OPTIMIZER_ARCHETYPE_AUDIT_20260919.md`. It is not a
full-search proof, and finite-energy Theory was deliberately not exercised.
`gaming_melt_seed_panel_diagnostic_20260919.json` is an independent
same-build seed-versus-ordinary check for its outlying Gaming formula residual.
